{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Submit to the tcb partition
#FLUX --queue=tcb

# The name of the job in the queue
#FLUX -J 5VKE_lb_25-122_0
# wall-clock time given to this job
#FLUX -t 23:30:00

# Number of nodes and number of MPI processes per node
#FLUX -N 1 -n 8 
# Request a GPU node and two GPUs (per node)
# Remove if you don't need a GPU
#FLUX -C gpu --gpus=2

# NOTE: SLURM's '--exclude' directive to avoid specific nodes has been omitted.

# excludes the unwanted nodes.

# Output file names for stdout and stderr
#FLUX -e job-{id}.err -o job-{id}.out

# NOTE: The --mail-user and --mail-type directives have been omitted as Flux

###YOU PROBABLY WANT TO EDIT STUFF BELOW HERE
module unload gromacs
module load gromacs/2020.5

var=0
time=23


var0=$((($var-1)))
if [ ! -f "step${var}.cpt" ]; then
	gmx grompp -maxwarn 1 -f ../../../../models/mdp/NPTres${var}.mdp  -c opt.gro  -p ../topol.top  -o topol${var}.tpr -n ../index.ndx -pp topol_pp.top -r opt.gro
    cmd="gmx mdrun -v -maxh $time -s topol${var}.tpr  -pin on -deffnm step$var "
	echo $cmd
	$cmd
	if [ ! -f "step${var}.gro" ]; then
        # 'sbatch' is replaced with 'flux submit' for job chaining.
		flux submit gromacs_tcb_${var}.sh
	else
		var=$((($var+1)))
		flux submit gromacs_tcb_${var}.sh
        fi 
else
    cmd="gmx mdrun -v -maxh $time -s topol${var}.tpr  -pin on -deffnm step$var -cpi step${var}.cpt"
    echo $cmd
    $cmd
	if [ ! -f "step${var}.gro" ]; then
		flux submit gromacs_tcb_${var}.sh
	else
		var=$((($var+1)))
		flux submit gromacs_tcb_${var}.sh
        fi 
fi
"
}

issues: The job requests resources for 8 parallel tasks (`#FLUX -n 8`), but the main computational step (`gmx mdrun ...`) is executed as a single serial command. It is not launched with a parallel runner like `flux run`. This will result in only one of the 8 allocated tasks being used, leaving the other 7 tasks completely idle and wasting the majority of the allocated CPU resources. To utilize the parallel allocation, the command should be launched with `flux run`, e.g., `flux run gmx mdrun ...`.

There is a potential mismatch between the number of tasks requested (8) and the number of GPUs requested (2). The GROMACS application (`gmx mdrun`) will have 8 MPI ranks competing for 2 GPUs, which can lead to complex GPU sharing scenarios, potential performance degradation, or errors, depending on how GROMACS and the system are configured to handle this. The resource request should be carefully aligned with the application's expected parallelization model (e.g., 2 tasks with 1 GPU each).
